content.comment_body: Hello, Counter settings: • ON at 10 or above; • OFF at 0; I performed an increment, and when 10 was reached it turned ON as expected. Then, after decrementing, when it reached 0, there was no change—the counter stayed ON even though it should have turned OFF. Is there something I'm missing?

The main issue seems to be that the online help for the counter was not consulted. If the ON value is greater than or equal to the OFF value, then Q turns ON when the count is greater than or equal to ON, and Q turns OFF only when the count is less than OFF—not when it is equal to OFF. Therefore, you should use 1 as your OFF value, not 0. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced counter behavior that did not match their expectations; although the counter activated correctly when reaching the ON value, it did not deactivate at the OFF value. The response clarified how the counter logic functions, highlighting a subtle detail in the threshold conditions for switching OFF. The interaction underlines the importance of documentation for understanding such features.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated that the counter would deactivate at the precise count set as the OFF value.
